messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug is related to reading CPIO archives generated by Redline RPM, which produce a non-zero file mode on the trailer entry. The failure occurs as an IllegalArgumentException when reading these archives. Inspecting the code of `CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextCPIOEntry()` method shows that it reads entries and returns null for the trailer entry, effectively ending iteration.

The detailed reading occurs in `readNewEntry(boolean hasCrc)`, which parses a new format CPIO entry from the input stream. It reads the mode value as an ASCII long. The code explicitly checks if the mode is zero and the entry is not the trailer — if the mode is zero and it's not the trailer entry, an IOException is thrown. However, there is no check or adjustment for non-zero modes on the trailer entry.

The issue described in the report is that the trailer entry generated by Redline RPM has a non-zero mode, which causes the code to proceed and treat the trailer entry as a normal entry instead of recognizing it as the trailer. This leads to an IllegalArgumentException or IOException when subsequent processing expects the trailer to have mode zero.

Therefore, the bug is due to missing handling for the case where the trailer entry has a non-zero file mode. The `readNewEntry` method expects mode zero for the trailer but Redline RPM violates this expectation, which the current code does not tolerate.

Suggested fix would be to allow or ignore non-zero modes on the trailer entry name to avoid throwing an error in this scenario. This explains the failure in the test `testCpioUnarchiveCreatedByRedlineRpm` reading the `redline.cpio` test archive.

The location of the bug is in the method `CpioArchiveInputStream.readNewEntry(boolean)` where the mode and trailer checks are done.

Next, I can suggest which methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.readNewEntry(boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
